coverage_observations.observation: zip assertions cover two successes, two domain failures with left-error precedence, and both branches starting. Neither one-sided domain failure is asserted. This is a small optional teaching extension for the right-error match arm, not a contradiction of the stated example scope or a demonstrated implementation defect.

correctness_checks.result: Success chain yields ready:11 and invokes double then increment; an initial DomainError bypasses both bind callbacks. Reassociation compares the same pure validate/format functions for a success and a failure; these are examples, not a general proof of monad laws.

Error formatting matches GaError.ToString; successful mapError never invokes its callback. Some 0 is present and subsequently fails explicit positive-value validation. None becomes the supplied error. Result.toOption intentionally erases distinct errors.
An IOException raised inside the supplied async workflow is caught and retained as IoError with its message and exception object. The assertions test that specific boundary.

All children are started before their handles are awaited. Successful values and returned errors are collected in input order. Empty and all-success lists yield Ok; mixed and all-error lists yield PartialFailure. The two integer unbox operations match the homogeneous input type and the source boxes successful values only in PartialFailure.

Async.Parallel evaluates both operands and retains array input order. Both Ok values are boxed internally then unboxed to their own generic types. Returned errors select the left error first, then the right error when only it fails.

fanOutAll has no exception-to-GaError catch. A raw child IOException escapes; wrapping the same kind of failure with fromAsync converts it into a collected IoError. The try/catch and wrapped assertions correctly distinguish those outcomes.
